questions.question: Which two sounds in English do NOT exist in Norwegian and are often hard for Norwegians?
questions.explanation: The unvoiced /θ/ (as in "think") and voiced /ð/ (as in "this") do not exist in Norwegian, so many Norwegians replace them with /t/, /s/ or /d/.

questions.question: A Norwegian speaker says "vine" when they mean "wine". Which pronunciation problem is this?
questions.explanation: Norwegian has no /w/ sound, so many Norwegians replace it with /v/. But "wine" and "vine" are completely different words!

questions.question: What are "minimal pairs"?
options: Two words that differ by only one sound, like "think" and "sink"
Two words that mean the same thing
The two shortest words in a sentence
questions.explanation: Minimal pairs are word pairs that differ in only one sound. Practising them helps you hear and produce difficult sound contrasts.

questions.question: Which words in a sentence usually receive stress (are emphasised)?
options: Content words like nouns, verbs and adjectives
Function words like articles and prepositions
questions.explanation: In English sentence stress, content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives) are stressed, while function words (articles, prepositions, pronouns) are usually unstressed.

questions.question: Which type of intonation is typically used in a yes/no question like "Are you coming?"
questions.explanation: Yes/no questions usually have rising intonation, while statements and wh-questions usually have falling intonation.
